placements.note: Structure preview: both 51–53 Christopher Street exteriors, including the current visitor-center storefront. Adjacent taller properties and interiors excluded; rear roof details approximate. Current source qa.json records completed review when available.

review.method: Exact inspected creator CC0 original plus independent primary historic/restored architectural descriptions and documented2024entry adaptation.
review.notes: Full fixed51–53ChristopherStreet exterior accepted at the agreed approximate medium-fi scope. Cleared Qualla images were checked first; exact4080x3072BakedintheHole2025creator CC0 photograph verifies53. Primary NYC LPC report LP-2574 independently describes both stable-derived buildings, their three/four upper casement bays and iron baskets, scored stucco, slightly different parapet heights,51rear wing, chimney/four skylights, brick storefronts and arched doors. Restoring architects EDG describe preserving the historic exterior and matching its original stucco scoring, then adapting51as the2024visitor center with accessibility upgrades. The firsthand2024opening account reports lowering its stoop. Corrected that concrete discrepancy:51now has a physical segmental recess, paired leaves and lowered model-street-datum sill; obsolete raised rounded stoop and continuous base strip across the doorway removed. All53geometry, roof/back/upper architecture, native footprints, USGS bare-earth ground and global placement remain exact. Portal width/head height retained; inferred lower threshold, opening depth, door pane pattern, roof equipment and unseen side/rear details remain explicit medium-fi estimates, not a measured accessibility or as-built survey. No private/copyrighted image or photo pixels used; full original scope retained.

candidates.caption: Outside of the official business district, the Stonewall Inn, a gay bar on Christopher Street in Manhattan's Greenwich Village. A 1969 police raid here led to the Stonewall riots, one of the most important events in the history of LGBT rights (and the history of the United States). This picture was taken on pride weekend in 2016, the day after President Obama announced the Stonewall National Monument, and less than two weeks after the Pulse nightclub shooting in Orlando.
Stonewall Inn, NYC (May 2014)

The Northern Dispensary at 167 Waverly Place where it intersects Grove Street and Christoper Street in the Greenwich Village neighborhood of Manhattan, New York City, was built in 1831 in the Federal style, with a third floor added in 1855. It was a private medical clinic for the poor, started in 1824.  It is located within the Greenwich Village Historic District. (Source: Guide to NYC Landmarks (4th ed.)) The building is triangular, due to the way the streets around it intersect.
